answer: Each identity must complete a chain of modular squarings, with each square depending on the previous result; a Wesolowski proof lets peers verify the work efficiently. An attacker can run cedar, dune, and juniper clones on separate hardware, but cannot split a single chain across GPUs to bypass its sequential delay. Sybil identities therefore require separate chains and real elapsed time, creating a physical bottleneck rather than a mere account-creation cost.
